sentence: 同事做錯嘢推畀我，搞到我要食死貓！
jyutping: tung4 si6 zou6 co3 je5 teoi1 bei2 ngo5, gaau2 dou3 ngo5 jiu3 sik6 sei2 maau1!
meaning_zh: 同事做錯事推給我，害我要背黑鍋！
meaning_en: My colleague messed up and pushed it onto me, leaving me to take the fall!
cultural_note: A very common workplace slang expression in Hong Kong.
author: WorkplaceSurvivor

sentence: 伙計，呢張檯埋單唔該，請問可唔可以用八達通？
jyutping: fo2 gei3, ni1 zoeng1 toi2 maai4 daan1 m4 goi1, cing2 man6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 jung6 baat3 daat6 tung1?
meaning_zh: 店員，這桌結帳麻煩了，請問可以用八達通付款嗎？
meaning_en: Waiter, bill for this table please, can I pay with Octopus card?
cultural_note: Originates from Cantonese commercial bookkeeping where accounts were tallied together (埋).
author: WanChaiLocal

sentence: 唔該幫我沖杯熱奶茶，少甜吖！
jyutping: m4 goi1 bong1 ngo5 cung1 bui1 jit6 naai5 caa4, siu2 tim4 aa1!
meaning_zh: 麻煩幫我泡一杯熱奶茶，微糖喔！
meaning_en: Please make me a hot milk tea, less sweet please!
cultural_note: '唔該' is universally used when asking for assistance or service in Cha Chaan Tengs.
author: ChaChaanTengFan

sentence: 炎炎夏日去茶餐廳，梗係要叫杯凍檸茶少甜走冰啦！
jyutping: jim4 jim4 haa6 jat6 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1, gang2 hai6 jiu3 giu3 bui1 dung3 ning4 caa4 siu2 tim4 zau2 bing1 laa1!
meaning_zh: 大熱天去茶餐廳，當然要點一杯凍檸茶微糖去冰啦！
meaning_en: On a scorching summer day in a tea restaurant, of course you must order an iced lemon tea, less sweet, no ice!
cultural_note: '走冰' (zau2 bing1) means no ice, and '少甜' (siu2 tim4) means less sugar.
author: HKFoodieGuide

sentence: 呢間餅店嘅酥皮蛋撻熱辣辣啱啱出爐，蛋香好濃郁！
jyutping: ni1 gaan1 beng2 dim3 ge3 sou1 pei4 daan6 taat3 jit6 laat6 laat6 aam1 aam1 ceot1 lou4, daan6 hoeng1 hou2 nung4 juk1!
meaning_zh: 這家餅店的酥皮蛋撻熱騰騰剛出爐，蛋香非常濃郁！
meaning_en: The flaky puff pastry egg tarts here are piping hot fresh from the oven, with such rich aroma!
cultural_note: Hong Kong egg tarts come in two main crusts: puff pastry (酥皮) and cookie crust (牛油皮).
author: BakeryLover852

sentence: 你好呀，好耐冇見，最近忙緊咩呀？
jyutping: nei5 hou2 aa3, hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3, zeoi3 gan6 mong4 gan2 me1 aa3?
meaning_zh: 你好呀，好久不見，最近在忙什麼呀？
meaning_en: Hello! Long time no see, what have you been up to recently?
cultural_note: A warm, natural conversational opener when bumping into friends in Hong Kong.
author: AhMing_HK
